revision_summary: No fabricated/mismatched quotes were found — all quotes check out against the transcript. The core issues are interpretive overreach and schema misuse, concentrated around the mobile-home/brick-underpinning thread. Required fixes: (1) Soften the outcome_dispute — the DQ is doubly grounded (mobile home AND no ground-mount capability, both confirmed independently), so 'the DQ may be premature' overstates the case; reframe as a settled-correct DQ with an open policy question for Kenny about underpinning exceptions, not a live dispute. (2) Re-scope cherry_pick_moments[3] (01:31, 'objection_inversion_miss') — multi_angle_resilience/objection_inversion per schema apply to cost/time/interest objections, not hard structural DQs; either drop this classification or relabel as a simple delivery/tone note. (3) Re-scope cherry_pick_moments[4] (01:49, 'knowledge_gap' under setter_scope_discipline) — the rep is explaining a legitimate DQ rationale, not engaging in closer-tier technical debate; setter_scope_discipline's anti-patterns are about debating specs to keep the customer engaged, not delivering a DQ reason with disfluency. Reclassify or drop. (4) Re-scope cherry_pick_moments[5] (02:03, 'enthusiasm_signal' under cross_sell_signals) — schema's cross_sell_signals section is populated only with roof_replacement_planned; ground-mount preference is not a recognized cross-sell trigger and should be flagged as a TBD schema gap candidate, not cited against the existing schema_reference as if already covered. (5) Add two missed intro-quality moments: 00:01 ('Hey, Debbie?') — rep guesses wrong name before company intro, and 00:06 ('Kimberly, I'm looking for Debbie Clark...') — rep asks for the lead before introducing herself/ION, delaying legitimacy establishment; both are relevant to why script_coverage marks intro_legitimacy as merely 'partial' and should be surfaced in starting_state or rep_intent. (6) Tone down coaching_focus priority-1 language that casts the underpinning question as "the single moment where the call's outcome is most contestable" — given the independent ground-mount hard gate, this overstates the stakes of an otherwise clean, brief DQ call.
